claims.claim_text: Sir Kenelm Digby (1603–65) spent the year 1628 as a privateer in the Mediterranean. During his time at sea he not only performed notable feats of heroism but wrote an autobiographical romance titled Loose Fantasies on the island of Milos. This essay offers a new account of the historical significance of Digby’s voyage and of the literary activities woven through it. His decision to sail to the Mediterranean is placed within the context both of his individual biography and of the upsurge of nostalgia for Elizabethan naval prowess in

research_value.meaning: Usefulness for further historical research; independent from evidential strength.

evidence_confidence.label: DISCOVERY_ONLY

retention.rule: Scientific triage may change automation priority but must not delete or hide the discovery.

supporting_evidence.warning: Discovery/OCR context is not an exact historical quotation.

confirmation_requirements: Inspect the original page/folio or authoritative facsimile.
Record an exact locator and controlled transcription.
Assess source genealogy before counting corroboration as independent.
Record limitations and claim scope before final verification.
falsification_targets: A primary or demonstrably independent contemporary source that directly contradicts the claim.
Evidence that the cited source refers to a different person, place, date, or event.
Evidence that apparently independent supporting sources derive from the same underlying source.
claims.rule: Absence of contradicting evidence is not proof that none exists.

rules: Every claim must remain traceable to preserved evidence.
Supporting-source count is not equivalent to independent corroboration.
Contradictory evidence and unknowns must be recorded explicitly.
Catalogue metadata and OCR discovery context cannot by themselves establish VERIFIED.
No automated stage may mark a claim VERIFIED.
Research Value and Evidence Confidence are separate; low confidence never deletes a research lead.
